question: Which permanent filesystem policy contract should OpenClaw adopt, and may its first version exclude shell-mediated filesystem access while still being presented as a security boundary?
rationale: The two open candidates are materially different config designs, and both leave exec able to bypass path restrictions; automation cannot choose the product guarantee or acceptable false-assurance risk.

options.title: Canonical file policy with explicit exec boundary
options.body: Select one `tools.fs` contract, land complete file and media enforcement, and clearly name arbitrary exec as outside the guarantee until separately contained.

options.title: Require exec containment in v1
options.body: Do not ship granular filesystem controls until shell-mediated reads and writes are constrained by an enforceable OS or runtime mechanism.

options.title: Keep OS isolation authoritative
options.body: Reject a granular core policy and continue directing strong isolation requirements to sandboxing, containers, virtual machines, or separate OS users.

recommendation.title: Canonical file policy with explicit exec boundary
recommendation.body: Select one `tools.fs` contract, land complete file and media enforcement, and clearly name arbitrary exec as outside the guarantee until separately contained.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the existing policy and have already framed the unresolved security boundary in this issue.
